name: esper blink

winrate_basis.why: no head-to-head winrate exists for Modern in any source this repo can reach: statistics_matchups returns zero rows for the format, statistics_archetypes carries no winrate field, and this run's own fingerprint records winrate_vs_field as all-zero. Recording a number here would be inventing one.

opponent_gameplan: Blink Solitude, Witch Enchanter and Overlord of the Balemurk with Ephemerate and Phelia for incremental value, with Thoughtseize stripping the cascade spell before it is cast.

opponent_plan.posture_why: Ephemerate loops on Solitude and Overlord of the Balemurk accrue cards rather than tempo; the dossier records their pressure as too slow to punish a slow start, so they win on value.

key_cards.why: recurs cards out of the graveyard every turn, which is the engine the card advantage actually comes from
one mana that repeats an enters trigger twice, turning each blink target into a two-for-one
free removal with lifegain that answers our returned bodies one at a time without spending a card in tempo
strips the cascade spell so the value engine never has to race anything

primary_gameplan: Hold the graveyard hate for their engine rather than their yard, protect one cascade, and present four bodies faster than their blink value accrues.
pitfalls: Committing everything to one Living End into three open mana and Wrath of the Skies.
Cycling Street Wraith into Thoughtseize range while holding both cascade spells.
Using Subtlety on a blinked Solitude, which is a trigger from a permanent already on the battlefield, not a creature spell.
stance_rationale: Overlord of the Balemurk and Emperor of Bones make their graveyard the engine, and Consign to Memory is the card that beats the cascade, so both answers earn a slot.

opposing_sideboard_in.why: one mana for the cascade trigger, the cheapest answer anyone has to this deck
taxes Shardless Agent and both free blue pitch spells
mills and exiles our graveyard every turn, which is a permanent answer rather than a one-shot
an X sweeper that scales to exile the Living End board at instant-speed-relevant timing

play_plan.keep: Two cyclers plus a cascade spell; their clock is slow enough that setup keeps are fine here.
play_plan.goldfish_for: One protected cascade - Dispute mana first, graveyard second.
play_plan.watch_for: Phelia exiling on attack means our returned bodies are not safe; Solitude means the biggest one is gone.
play_plan.posture_why: their pressure is too slow to punish a slow start.
